name: St. Joseph
tags: patron of the universal Church, fathers, workers
bio: Husband of Mary and foster father of Jesus. A quiet, faithful carpenter who protected the Holy Family.

name: St. Peter
bio: A fisherman Jesus called to be the "rock" of his Church. Leader of the Apostles and the first Bishop of Rome, martyred in Rome.

name: St. Paul
bio: Once a persecutor of Christians, he met the risen Christ and became the great missionary to the Gentiles. His letters fill much of the New Testament.

name: St. Patrick
bio: Kidnapped as a teenager and enslaved in Ireland, he escaped, became a priest and returned to bring the Gospel to the Irish people.

name: St. Augustine of Hippo
tags: Doctor of the Church, bishop, convert
bio: After a restless youth, he was converted through the prayers of his mother, St. Monica. His Confessions is one of the most-read books in history.

name: St. Benedict of Nursia
bio: Wrote the Rule that shaped Western monastic life around prayer and work: ora et labora.

name: St. Francis of Assisi
bio: A wealthy young man who gave up everything to follow Christ in poverty. Founder of the Franciscans and lover of all God's creatures. Canonized 1228.

name: St. Clare of Assisi
bio: Friend and follower of St. Francis who founded the Poor Clares, a community of contemplative sisters.

name: St. Thomas Aquinas
tags: Doctor of the Church, students, theologian
bio: Dominican friar and the Church's great theologian, author of the Summa Theologiae. Canonized 1323.

name: St. Catherine of Siena
tags: Doctor of the Church, mystic, patron of Europe
bio: A laywoman and mystic who cared for the sick and boldly urged the Pope to return to Rome. Canonized 1461.

name: St. Joan of Arc
bio: A peasant girl who, guided by heavenly voices, led the French army before being burned at the stake at 19. Canonized 1920.

name: St. Ignatius of Loyola
bio: A wounded soldier who found God while recovering and founded the Society of Jesus (Jesuits). Canonized 1622.

name: St. Teresa of Ávila
tags: Doctor of the Church, prayer, mystic
bio: Carmelite reformer and one of the great teachers of prayer, author of The Interior Castle. Canonized 1622.

name: St. Juan Diego
bio: An Indigenous Mexican man to whom Our Lady of Guadalupe appeared in 1531, leaving her image on his cloak. Canonized 2002.

name: St. Rose of Lima
bio: A young Peruvian laywoman of deep prayer and penance who served the poor. The first canonized saint of the Americas (1671).

name: St. Martin de Porres
bio: Son of a Spanish nobleman and a freed slave, this Dominican brother in Lima cared for the sick and poor of every race. Canonized 1962.

name: St. Kateri Tekakwitha
bio: A Mohawk-Algonquin woman who embraced the faith despite opposition. The first Native American saint, canonized 2012.

name: St. Junípero Serra
bio: Franciscan missionary who founded the first nine of California's missions. Canonized 2015.

name: St. Elizabeth Ann Seton
bio: A New York wife and mother, widowed young, who became Catholic and founded the Sisters of Charity. The first U.S.-born saint, canonized 1975.

name: St. John Neumann
bio: Bohemian immigrant who became Bishop of Philadelphia and built the first diocesan Catholic school system in the U.S. Canonized 1977.

name: St. Damien of Molokai
bio: Belgian priest who served the leprosy colony on Molokai, Hawaii, and died of the disease himself. Canonized 2009.

name: St. Marianne Cope
bio: Franciscan sister from New York who cared for leprosy patients on Molokai for 30 years. Canonized 2012.

name: St. Frances Xavier Cabrini
bio: Italian missionary who founded schools, orphanages and hospitals for immigrants in America. The first U.S. citizen to be canonized (1946).

name: St. Katharine Drexel
bio: A Philadelphia heiress who gave her fortune and life to serve Black and Native American communities. Canonized 2000.

name: St. Thérèse of Lisieux
tags: Doctor of the Church, missions, the Little Way
bio: A French Carmelite nun who taught the "little way" of doing small things with great love. Died at 24. Canonized 1925.

name: St. Josephine Bakhita
bio: Kidnapped and enslaved as a child in Sudan, she found freedom and faith in Italy and became a Canossian sister. Canonized 2000.

name: St. Maximilian Kolbe
bio: Polish Franciscan priest who offered his life in place of a stranger at Auschwitz. Canonized 1982.

name: St. Faustina Kowalska
bio: Polish nun whose diary of visions of Jesus spread devotion to the Divine Mercy. Canonized 2000.

name: St. Pio of Pietrelcina (Padre Pio)
bio: Capuchin friar famed for long hours in the confessional, deep prayer and the stigmata. Canonized 2002.

name: St. Gianna Beretta Molla
bio: Italian pediatrician, wife and mother who chose to save her unborn daughter's life at the cost of her own. Canonized 2004.

name: St. Teresa of Calcutta
bio: Founder of the Missionaries of Charity, who served the poorest of the poor in Calcutta and worldwide. Canonized 2016.

name: St. Óscar Romero
bio: Archbishop of San Salvador who spoke out for the poor and was shot while celebrating Mass. Canonized 2018.

name: St. John Paul II
bio: Polish pope for nearly 27 years, who traveled the world, helped bring down communism in Europe and began World Youth Day. Canonized 2014.

name: St. John Henry Newman
bio: Anglican priest and Oxford scholar who became Catholic and later a cardinal. Canonized 2019.

name: St. Pier Giorgio Frassati
bio: Italian student and mountaineer who quietly served the poor of Turin. Canonized September 7, 2025.

name: St. Carlo Acutis
bio: Italian teenager and computer whiz who built a website cataloging Eucharistic miracles. Died of leukemia at 15. Canonized September 7, 2025.

name: Bl. Miguel Pro
bio: Mexican Jesuit who ministered in secret during persecution and was executed crying "Viva Cristo Rey!" Beatified 1988.

name: Bl. Franz Jägerstätter
bio: Austrian farmer, husband and father executed for refusing to fight for the Nazis. Beatified 2007.

name: Bl. Chiara Badano
bio: Italian teenager who faced bone cancer with radiant joy, offering her suffering to Jesus. Beatified 2010.

name: Bl. Solanus Casey
bio: Capuchin friar who served as a humble doorkeeper in Detroit, where thousands came for his counsel and prayers. Beatified 2017.

name: Bl. Stanley Rother
bio: Oklahoma priest who served the people of Santiago Atitlán, Guatemala, and was murdered there. The first U.S.-born martyr to be beatified (2017).

name: Bl. Michael McGivney
tags: United States, Knights of Columbus, fathers
bio: Connecticut parish priest who founded the Knights of Columbus to support Catholic families. Beatified 2020.

name: Ven. Pierre Toussaint
bio: Born enslaved in Haiti, he became a renowned New York hairdresser and a generous benefactor of the poor and orphans. Declared Venerable 1996.

name: Ven. Mary Elizabeth Lange
bio: Founded the Oblate Sisters of Providence in Baltimore, the first lasting community of Black Catholic sisters. Declared Venerable 2023.

name: Ven. Henriette Delille
bio: Free woman of color in New Orleans who founded the Sisters of the Holy Family to serve the enslaved, the poor and the elderly. Declared Venerable 2010.

name: Ven. Augustus Tolton
bio: Born enslaved in Missouri, he became the first recognizably Black priest in the U.S. after studying in Rome. Declared Venerable 2019.

name: Ven. Fulton J. Sheen
bio: Archbishop and Emmy-winning TV preacher whose programs brought the faith to millions of Americans. Declared Venerable 2012.

name: Ven. Patrick Peyton
bio: Irish-born priest famous for the motto "The family that prays together stays together." Declared Venerable 2017.

name: Ven. Jérôme Lejeune
bio: French geneticist who discovered the cause of Down syndrome and defended the dignity of every human life. Declared Venerable 2021.

name: Servant of God Julia Greeley
bio: Born enslaved, she became a beloved figure in Denver, pulling a red wagon of food and clothing to the poor at night. Cause opened 2016.

name: Servant of God Nicholas Black Elk
bio: Lakota holy man who became Catholic and served for decades as a catechist among his people. Cause opened 2017.

name: Servant of God Dorothy Day
tags: United States, New York, the poor, converts
bio: Journalist and convert who co-founded the Catholic Worker movement and its houses of hospitality. Cause opened 2000.

name: Servant of God Thea Bowman
bio: Franciscan sister, teacher and singer who shared the gifts of Black Catholic culture with the whole Church. Cause opened 2018.
